name: Agent bank accounts compared
description: Agent-owned or agent-attributed deposit accounts and bank-issued agent payment credentials. Not documented means the linked page does not state the fact. Rows are alphabetical by product.
attribution: The Agent Economy agent bank accounts (https://theagenteconomy.si/data/agent-bank-accounts.json), licensed under CC BY 4.0.
inclusion: A row is an agent-owned or agent-attributed deposit account, or an agent payment credential issued through a bank. The provider's own pages must describe that account or credential. Sandbox-only registration, BIN sponsorship, an on-chain balance, merchant payout to a seller account, and human-approved access to an existing business account are left out. Cells quote the linked page.
title: Agent bank accounts compared

account_type.text: Scoped account numbers attributed to end users' agents. The page says each is a unique account number, and the account number example on the page includes a routing number. The blog says the number is created on the underlying entity's account.
account_type.source_title: Agent Account Numbers for Agentic Finance
account_type.note: The blog Moving money with agents describes the underlying entity account.

who_can_open.text: A company can provision an account number for an agent or task through Lead's Account Number API. POST /v1/account_number creates the number and can assign a client_customer_id or an entity_id. The pages describe a bank API for companies, not a consumer signup.
who_can_open.note: Managing Account Numbers documents the create call and the optional client_customer_id or entity_id.

rails.text: ACH, wires (including outgoing international wires), instant payments, and internal transfers, through the controls API. The product page also says agents can transact across ACH, wire, instant payments, and blockchain through Lead's APIs.
rails.note: Blockchain is named on the product page, not in the controls field list.

controls.text: Per-rail incoming and outgoing controls, including accept_credit and accept_debit on ACH, and a counterparty_filter of accept_all, reject_all, or allowlist_only with allowlists. The product page says OFAC and sanctions screening runs at intent, and that every action is checked in real time against account balances, velocity limits, and bank-enforced spend ceilings the business has configured. The blog names daily and monthly limits agreed at program setup. The controls doc does not list a numeric ceiling field.
controls.note: Spend ceilings and daily or monthly limits are on the product page and the blog.

agent_can_change_rules.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-16. PATCH /v1/account_number/{id} updates controls or metadata. The Managing Account Numbers and Controls pages do not say whether an agent is given that API credential.

revocation.text: Deactivate an active account number so it can no longer send or receive, and later activate it again. Cancel is permanent, and the number is not recycled.

stated_liability.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-16. The product page, controls doc, managing doc, and blog were checked and do not state a liability rule for agent payments.
stated_liability.source_title: Agent Account Numbers for Agentic Finance

status.text: Live. The product page does not label the offering as preview or beta.
status.source_title: Agent Account Numbers for Agentic Finance

account_type.text: A Natural wallet the agent pays from. Natural is a financial technology company, not a bank. Wallet Accounts and banking services are provided by Column N.A., Member FDIC. Deposits in Wallet accounts are FDIC-insured through Column N.A. and Column's Sweep Program Network Banks, if the stated conditions are met.
account_type.note: The same Column and FDIC sentences are on the Natural wallet page.

who_can_open.text: Any verified business on Natural with a funded wallet can use Direct, through the Natural API, SDKs, CLI, or the payments MCP.

rails.text: ACH, domestic wire, and realtime over RTP and FedNow, from the same wallet. International wires (SWIFT) and checks are described as coming soon.
rails.note: The Direct changelog dated October 21, 2026 names ACH, domestic wire, and realtime powered by RTP and FedNow.

controls.text: Per-transaction, per-day, and per-month spend limits at the account and agent levels, plus a connection limit a customer may set. The set limits guide says that customer level is per transaction only. A payment that breaches a limit is held for approval. The limits overview says a limit never automatically fails a payment, while Natural program policies can decline a payment. Direct payments cannot exceed the agent's wallet balance. Payees are screened before a payment may be sent, and Natural checks whether the account can receive that rail.
controls.note: The holds rule is on the limits overview. Balance and payee screening are on the Direct page.

agent_can_change_rules.text: No. The limits overview says an agent can read the caps that gate it but can never set, raise, or remove them. PUT /parties/me/limits requires party.update, and the set limits guide says agent keys cannot call it.
agent_can_change_rules.note: The party.update restriction is on the set limits guide.

revocation.text: A Direct payment can be canceled before it is sent to the bank. The Direct page says an agent or the user can cancel while it is queued or waiting for approval. An approval hold can be denied, or the held movement canceled, and an agent can never clear a hold. The disclosures page says you may revoke an AI agent's access at any time in the Natural Dashboard. A close of the wallet itself is not stated on the Direct, MCP, approvals, or disclosures pages.
revocation.note: MCP cancel_direct_payment, the approvals guide, and the disclosures page were also checked.

stated_liability.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-16. The Direct page, the wallet page, and the limits pages do not state a liability rule. The disclosures page points to a Wallet Account Agreement. That agreement was not loaded as a separate document.

status.text: Live. The October 29, 2026 post says Direct is in general availability. The Direct page does not label the product as preview or beta.

account_type.text: A dedicated stablecoin wallet, IBAN, and card that belong to the agent, kept separate from the user's personal accounts. The about page says Navoka is powered by Wirex. The Agent Terms say the Service is software from Wirex Holdings Limited, while accounts, IBANs, cards, and payments are provided by a separate Wirex group company under Provider Terms.
account_type.note: The about page and Agent Terms were also checked.

who_can_open.text: You must be at least 18 and legally able to enter a contract, for yourself or a business you are authorized to bind. A chat or assistant sign-in creates the account, which can hold and send USDC and EURC right away. The IBAN and card require a one-time identity check, or a Wirex One connection that imports verification. The about page says eligibility is confirmed during sign-in before any identity documents are requested, and that accounts are in dollars, euro, and pounds.
who_can_open.note: The home page, about page, and Wirex One page describe sign-in and the identity import.

rails.text: ACH, SEPA, Faster Payments, SWIFT, stablecoin, and a debit card. The about and home pages also mention push-to-card.
rails.note: The home page lists the same rails and push-to-card.

controls.text: A holder-set policy: monthly budget, approve-above threshold, per-transaction ceiling, velocity as count and value per window, payee and merchant allowlist, country list, MCC allow and deny, and a kill switch. Payments inside the rules can run unattended or wait, depending on the mode. Anything outside is held. Sample amounts on the controls page are not stated as product defaults.
controls.note: Agent Terms section 3.2 names the same policy fields.

agent_can_change_rules.text: No. The controls page and Agent Terms section 3.2 say the agent can read the policy and cannot change it. The set_policy tool is holder-only. An agent or assistant session calling it is refused and logged.
agent_can_change_rules.note: Agent Terms section 3.2 states the same rule.

revocation.text: A kill switch freezes cards, pauses rules, and unlinks assistants immediately. Unpausing restores the rules as they were. You can disconnect the agent at any time. Ending the Agent Terms does not close the Provider account. Closing the account is under the Provider Terms.
revocation.note: Agent Terms sections 3.5 and 11 cover the kill switch, disconnect, and account closing.

stated_liability.text: Subject to clause 10.1, which keeps non-excludable legal rights, Wirex Holdings is not liable for acts or omissions of the Provider, a messaging platform, a third-party assistant, or a merchant; for losses from instructions you gave or approved, or from a Policy you set; or for losses from AI output you did not check before approving. Total liability under those terms in any 12-month period is limited to the greater of 100 pounds sterling and the software fees paid in that period. The Service has no software fee. These are software terms. Execution, settlement, reversals, chargebacks, fees, and limits are governed by the Provider Terms, which were not loaded as a separate document.

status.text: Live. The Navoka pages checked on November 16, 2026 say eligibility is confirmed during sign-in and do not repeat an invitation-only limit. A Wirex release dated November 12, 2026 said the platform was accessible by invitation only.
status.note: The November 12, 2026 Wirex release is the invitation-only sentence.

account_type.text: Stripe Issuing cards and credentials for agents, including single-use virtual cards, Shared Payment Tokens, and agentic network tokens from Visa or Mastercard. This is card issuing, not a deposit account number.

who_can_open.text: Businesses apply in the Stripe Dashboard for cards for their own business, or contact Stripe for cards for a platform. The page says to apply or contact Stripe directly.

rails.text: Cards, plus programmatic checkout through MPP or UCP via a Shared Payment Token, and browser checkout with virtual card details.

controls.text: Spend controls and merchant category controls at the card or cardholder level, lifecycle controls for single-use cards, and real-time authorization decisioning that can approve or decline each purchase.

agent_can_change_rules.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-16. The page says you decide what the agent can spend, where, and how much. If the account has Issuing create methods through Stripe MCP, you can ask an agent to create cardholders and cards. The page does not say the agent can change spend controls.

revocation.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-16. A broader deactivate or cancel of the agent's issuing authority is not spelled out on the Issuing for agents page. The capabilities table says single-use cards are automatically invalidated after use.

stated_liability.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-16. The Issuing for agents page does not state a liability rule.

status.text: Beta. Stripe's Issuing for agents page labels the product Private preview.

account_type.text: Link returns a payment credential for a spend request. The default is a virtual card for one-time purchases, and recurring cards are also documented. The customer's real card or bank number is never exposed. Cross River Bank's July 1, 2026 newsroom post says that when an AI agent needs to make a purchase, Link's agent wallet issues a restricted, single-use virtual card scoped to that transaction, and that Cross River's banking core underpins the issuing.
account_type.note: The Cross River newsroom post is the issuing sentence.

who_can_open.text: A customer sets up a Link balance: agree to terms, an identity check with date of birth and the last four digits of a Social Security number, a per-purchase limit, and added money. The agent uses link-cli to create spend requests.
who_can_open.source_title: Set up a balance for agent wallet purchases
who_can_open.note: Enable agents to spend describes the spend request the agent creates.

rails.text: Virtual cards by default. The Enable agents to spend table also names Link Pay Tokens and shared payment tokens where the seller supports them. The README still documents Machine Payments Protocol pay with a shared payment token.
rails.note: The README credential types section names the shared payment token and Link Pay Token.

controls.text: The customer sets a per-purchase limit. Above that limit the agent cannot skip approval, and a limit of $0 prevents skipping. The link-cli README lists a maximum amount per spend request of $500 (50,000 cents), a daily spend of $500, and a 30-day spend of $20,000. Cross River describes the virtual card as restricted and scoped to that transaction.
controls.source_title: Set up a balance for agent wallet purchases
controls.note: The dollar caps are in the README limits table. Cross River's newsroom post uses the words restricted and scoped to that transaction.

agent_can_change_rules.text: No. To change the skip-approval limit, the customer asks the agent for a link and changes the amount on that page.
agent_can_change_rules.source_title: Set up a balance for agent wallet purchases

revocation.text: link-cli can cancel a spend request from the created, pending_approval, or approved state, which revokes the credential. The README says this does not cancel a merchant subscription. A revoke of the agent's overall spending authority is not stated on the support page.

stated_liability.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-16. The Enable agents to spend page, the README, and the support page do not state a liability rule.

status.text: Live. The Enable agents to spend page and the README do not label the spend request flow as preview or beta.

account_type.text: An agent connects to a business's Stripe Treasury account through Stripe's MCP server, using OAuth or an agent API key. This is access to the business's Treasury account, not a separate consumer account number.
account_type.note: The October 21, 2026 newsroom post describes the same Treasury account connection.

who_can_open.text: Businesses that use Stripe Treasury, subject to Treasury availability. The docs point to Stripe's Treasury availability page for where Treasury is available.

rails.text: The supported tools are get_balance_summary, convert_currency, send_money, setup_recipient, and transfer_money, each labeled Public preview. The newsroom describes checking balances, paying invoices, transferring funds, and converting currencies.
rails.note: The newsroom sentences are in the October 21, 2026 post.

controls.text: The account holder chooses the permission level for each capability. By default, the account holder must review and approve any agent action that results in live money movement. The October 21, 2026 newsroom post said businesses will soon be able to create cards and set spending limits for their agents in the coming weeks. The Treasury for agents docs checked on November 16, 2026 do not document those spend limits as generally available.
controls.note: The coming weeks sentence is only in the October 21, 2026 newsroom post.

agent_can_change_rules.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-16. The page says the account holder chooses permissions and, by default, reviews live money movement. It does not say the agent can change those permissions.

revocation.text: An administrator with team-management permission can revoke one OAuth session or all listed sessions for a team member, in the current account and environment, live mode or a sandbox.

stated_liability.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-16. The Treasury for agents docs and the newsroom post do not state a liability rule.

status.text: Beta. The Treasury for agents docs label the Treasury tools as Public preview.
